fact: UNICEF's national sub-office head says Chad has worked since 2021 to modernise civil registration through digitalisation and deployment of the TASDJIL application.
ANATS and the OIF discussed digitalisation and interoperability of civil registration services between communes and the SIGPTS, with ANATS issuing secure birth certificates in several provinces.
An ATPE opinion piece says the TASDJIL system of Technidev and ANATS already digitally registers births at a hospital desk at Koukou Angarana in Sila province, with experiences still to be scaled up.
TECHNIDEV's director general says civil registry desks have been set up in more than 50 maternity units under TASDJIL, with the aim of covering all health facilities.
An OIF-supported project running to June 2026 in N'Djamena, Batha and Hadjer Lamis aims to strengthen the TASDJIL digitisation system for birth registration.
The head of ANATS Abeche put Chad's birth registration rate at about 26 percent, not tied to a digital system.
Radio Ndarason reports a digital birth registration desk at Mongo provincial hospital, backed by the government and UNICEF, serving 18 health centres within 75 km and logging 10 to 15 births a day.
The World Bank's WDI lists completeness of birth registration in Chad at 25.7% for 2019, a national rate not tied to a digital system.
